genZNote: The other half of the yogurt duo, and the one that actually makes it taste like yogurt by pumping out lactic acid.

morphology.oxygenRequirement: Aerotolerant anaerobe (microaerophilic to anaerobic, tolerates some O2)

habitat.hostAssociation: Not a resident of normal human microbiota; used as a food-grade starter culture
habitat.environmentalOccurrence: Industrially propagated worldwide for yogurt production

culture.growthCharacteristics: Thermophilic (optimal ~40-45°C); produces large amounts of lactic acid
culture.colonyMorphology: Small, rough or smooth white colonies

identificationClues: Gram-positive rod, catalase-negative — fits the general Lactobacillus profile
Homofermentative, high lactic-acid producer, giving yogurt its characteristic tang
Grows optimally near 45°C alongside Streptococcus thermophilus in traditional yogurt culture
Not associated with human disease in normal dietary use

examFacts.keyBiochemicalReaction: Catalase negative; homofermentative lactic acid production
examFacts.distinguishingFeature: Partners with S. thermophilus as the classic yogurt starter culture pair
